h.strategy: Borrow interaction patterns from other empirical sciences: epistasis in genetics (the effect of one mutation depends on genetic background, and beneficial mutations help fitter backgrounds less), diminishing returns in economics, and redundancy in engineered systems. Translate each pattern into a concrete conditional hypothesis about how an edit's effect varies with the parent configuration. Favor predictions that a practitioner thinking only mechanistically would get wrong, especially background-dependent sign changes and weaker gains in already-strong parents. Use conditions that many parents satisfy. In the flaw step, discard analogies that do not transfer and keep only those with a plausible general reason to hold.

hyps.why: Completing an all-conv 0->1->2->3 chain adds compounding depth, so the edge-5 conv gain grows when edge 2 is already conv.
Restoring node 2's missing route to the output gives a much larger gain than upgrading an existing op, which yields zero gain when it is already conv.
Replacing the only direct identity shortcut sacrifices the residual path that eases optimization, so the conv's net gain is smaller than when it replaces none or pooling.
With edge 5 removed, the output depends more on the direct edge-3 path, so placing learned capacity there matters more.
An identity shortcut is most valuable alongside a deep conv path to the output, mirroring the ResNet effect, and costs more when the deep path is weak.
Swapping a learned conv for parameter-free pooling on edge 4 loses capacity, which is far worse than swapping out none or skip.
When node 2 also receives a conv branch via edge 1, learned features survive, so making edge 2 pooling is less harmful.
Pruning an unparameterized pooling edge removes blur from node 3's sum and costs little or helps, unlike pruning a conv or skip.
If edge 4 is already absent, removing edge 5 leaves only the direct edge-3 path to the output, collapsing the cell's depth and hurting much more.
With edge 5 removed, node 2 never reaches the output, so adding a conv on edge 1 into node 2 has little effect on accuracy.
